inspiration: Large winged creature idle: the head glance picks a new target on a half-second floored clock (a hashed offset per step), with a slow cosine breath on the chest and beak. The chest is pitched forward by a fixed amount in the wyvern branch. This makes the creature feel alive without per-frame noise (voxygen/anim/src/bird_large/idle.rs lines 27, 38, 66).

Creatures built from parts: each body plan has central parts and lateral (left/right) parts with offsets, and a wyvern wing is split into inner, middle and outer segments in the manifest (bird_large_lateral_manifest.ron line 425). Our rig can use the same split for wings and tails at our own proportions.

Combat music is driven by a crowd-weighted sum: every hostile inside a radius adds ceil(max HP / health factor) to a total; a high threshold selects the strongest combat state, and a dead player forces explore music (voxygen/src/audio/music.rs lines 264-285). This maps onto our many-on-one threat budget (MAX_ATTACKERS, hate list) as a sound signal.

Asymmetric crossfades: the combat-to-explore fade is slow in (5 s in, 2 s out), explore to combat is quick (1.0 s out, 0.5 s in), and an interrupt delay of 5 s stops rapid flip-flopping (music_transition_manifest.ron lines 13 and 16). Good shape for stingers and biome beds.

Talent prerequisites in one flat data file: each node says Any-of or All-of earlier nodes, so a capstone needs all of one earlier node and a branch needs one of two (skill_prerequisites.ron lines 2 and 4). Clear, data-only progression graph.

Creature loot as one All-of bundle with min and max counts per item (for example a scale stack of 8 to 12). Each creature file names its loot table by path (frostwyvern.ron line 7). Gives a readable 'materials ceremony' after a kill.

Credits register as data: every asset has authors, source link, licence, licence link and free-text notes, and a missing licence defaults to a stated repo licence. Good template for our own asset provenance file, with the default-to-copyleft rule written out.
Fluent localisation with plural variants (a selector on a count with [1] and *[other] branches) for HUD text that shows numbers, such as heal durations.

briefs.label: Pitched-chest winged wyrm (bird_large, wyvern branch)
briefs.why: A forward-pitched chest and a head that glances on a short beat make a winged monster read as watchful at 375 wide, even when it is still. The wing split into three segments gives a clear silhouette in motion.
briefs.keep: forward-pitched chest; head glance on a stepped clock; wing split into inner, middle and outer segments
briefs.change: our own wing count and shape (a sail, not a fore-wing and hind-wing pair); our palette, not the donor's ice motif; a crest or horn ornament in place of their head shape

briefs.label: Crowd-weighted combat bed (sound-music)
briefs.why: A threat sum that weights tougher enemies more and only counts those inside a radius is a simple, testable rule for when combat music starts. Asymmetric fades make the entry feel urgent and the exit feel earned.
briefs.keep: threat weight from max HP; radius gate; interrupt delay; quick cut in, slow fade out
briefs.change: weight from our hate list and MAX_ATTACKERS (not a radius sum); per-zone thresholds as data; a boss stinger on top of the bed rather than a second track

briefs.label: Branching blade talent line (progression)
briefs.why: A single flat table of Any-of and All-of prerequisites gives a readable talent tree with capstones and forks, and each rule is one line a designer can check.
briefs.keep: capstone needs All of one earlier node; a fork needs Any of two nodes; prerequisites in data
briefs.change: our node names and depth, costs per node, forks drawn across tiers rather than in one line; no copied node names

briefs.label: Material bundle drop (loot ceremony)
briefs.why: A boss or large creature that drops a stack of one material with a count range (not one item) reads as a reward on the loot screen and gives crafting a clear input.
briefs.keep: one bundle per creature; each entry a min and max count; All-of semantics
briefs.change: our material names and count ranges; add a rare tier roll on top; different ordering and icon treatment
